areas.core: Fundamentals of what a robot is and program structure

skills.label: Sense-decide-act loop
skills.def: A robot repeatedly senses its world, decides what to do, and acts.

skills.label: Sequence and order
skills.def: A program is an ordered list of steps that run one after another.

skills.label: Controlling an LED
skills.def: You can turn an output like an LED on and off from your program.

skills.label: Driving and turning
skills.def: Commands make the robot move forward and turn, changing where it points.

skills.label: Order matters
skills.def: The same steps in a different order make the robot do something different.

skills.label: Reading a symptom
skills.def: Watch what the robot actually does and describe the problem before guessing a cause.

skills.label: Debugging as a discipline
skills.def: Debugging is a repeatable method, not luck.

skills.label: Version control
skills.def: Track and document your work with version control.

skills.label: Counted loop
skills.def: A repeat block runs the same steps a fixed number of times.

skills.label: Nested loops
skills.def: A loop inside another loop repeats a whole pattern many times.

skills.label: Variables
skills.def: A variable is a named box that remembers a number for later.

skills.label: Parameterising with a value
skills.def: Using a variable instead of a fixed number lets one program make many results.

skills.label: Doing more with less
skills.def: A shorter program that gets the same result is usually a better program.

skills.label: Distance sensing
skills.def: A distance sensor reports how far away the nearest obstacle is.

skills.label: Choosing a threshold
skills.def: Pick a cutoff value that separates 'close enough to act' from 'not yet'.

skills.label: Sensor noise
skills.def: Real readings jitter and sometimes lie, so a single value cannot be trusted.

skills.label: Blind spots and cones
skills.def: A sensor only sees a limited cone and can miss angled walls or narrow gaps.

skills.label: Conditionals
skills.def: An if/else picks between actions based on whether a condition is true.

skills.label: Hysteresis
skills.def: Using two thresholds instead of one stops a robot flip-flopping on noisy readings.

skills.label: Isolating a fault
skills.def: Narrow down where a problem is by testing one piece of the program at a time.

skills.label: Voltage
skills.def: Voltage is the electrical push that drives current around a circuit.

skills.label: Current
skills.def: Current is the amount of electric charge flowing through a circuit.

skills.label: Ohm's law
skills.def: Voltage equals current times resistance, so a resistor limits the current.

skills.label: Power budgets
skills.def: A battery holds a limited charge, so you must budget how much current things draw.

skills.label: Battery safety
skills.def: Batteries can overheat or catch fire if shorted or mishandled, so follow safe rules.

skills.label: Gear ratios
skills.def: A gear ratio trades speed for turning force by dividing or multiplying rotation.

skills.label: Torque and speed
skills.def: Gears let a motor choose between more turning force and more speed, not both.

skills.label: Servo position control
skills.def: A servo moves to a commanded angle rather than just spinning at a speed.

skills.label: PWM duty cycle
skills.def: Switching power on and off quickly sets an average 'half speed' for a motor.

skills.label: Events and polling
skills.def: You can keep checking for something to happen, or wait to be told when it does.

skills.label: Interrupts
skills.def: An interrupt lets the robot react instantly to an event without polling for it.

skills.label: State machines
skills.def: A robot can be in one of several named states and switch between them on events.

skills.label: Functions
skills.def: A function is a named group of steps you can call and reuse.

skills.label: Abstraction
skills.def: Naming an idea as a function lets you use it without re-reading how it works.

skills.label: Tracing execution
skills.def: Follow the program step by step to see what value each part has as it runs.

skills.label: Code syntax
skills.def: Text code has strict rules for indentation, colons and spelling that must be exact.

skills.label: Functions with arguments
skills.def: A text function can take arguments and return a value back to the caller.

skills.label: Reading errors
skills.def: An error message names the line and the kind of mistake so you can fix it.

skills.label: Blocks to text
skills.def: The same program you built with blocks can be written and read as text code.

skills.label: Flashing hardware
skills.def: You can load your program onto a real board so it runs on real wheels.

skills.label: Sim-to-real gap
skills.def: Real hardware behaves differently from the simulator, and the difference is the lesson.

skills.label: Open-loop control
skills.def: Open-loop means commanding an action blindly, like 'drive for two seconds'.

skills.label: Closed-loop control
skills.def: Closed-loop means using a sensor to keep acting until the goal is actually reached.

skills.label: Error signal
skills.def: Error is the gap between where you are and where you want to be.

skills.label: Proportional control
skills.def: Correct by an amount proportional to the error: correction equals gain times error.

skills.label: Derivative term
skills.def: Reacting to how fast the error changes damps overshoot and wobble.

skills.label: Tuning method
skills.def: Tune by changing one gain, recording what happens, and repeating.

skills.label: Change one variable
skills.def: Change only one thing at a time so you know what caused the result.

skills.label: Coordinate frames
skills.def: Position is described with x, y and heading, in the world's or the robot's frame.

skills.label: Differential-drive kinematics
skills.def: Two wheel speeds combine to make the robot drive straight or curve along a path.

skills.label: Odometry
skills.def: Counting wheel ticks turns distance travelled into an estimate of position.

skills.label: Drift and slip
skills.def: Small errors in each step add up, so the robot slowly gets lost over time.

skills.label: Error budgets
skills.def: An error budget adds up where position error comes from and how big each source is.

skills.label: Forward kinematics of an arm
skills.def: Joint angles of a jointed arm determine where its tip ends up in space.

skills.label: Wheel encoders
skills.def: An encoder counts wheel ticks so you can measure how far a wheel has turned.

skills.label: IMU heading
skills.def: An IMU reports the robot's heading, though its estimate slowly drifts.

skills.label: Reactive strategies
skills.def: Reacting to what the sensor sees right now, like wall-following, always works but is often slow.

skills.label: The world as a grid
skills.def: Chopping the world into a grid of cells makes it something an algorithm can search.

skills.label: Breadth-first search
skills.def: Flood fill explores a grid outward from the start to find a path to the goal.

skills.label: Path cost
skills.def: Each move has a cost, and a good plan is the one with the lowest total cost.

skills.label: Heuristics
skills.def: A heuristic guesses which direction is promising so search does less wasted work.

skills.label: Replanning
skills.def: When the world changes mid-run, throw away the old plan and compute a new one.

skills.label: Cost of computation
skills.def: Some approaches take far more steps than others as the problem grows.

skills.label: Pixels and images
skills.def: A camera gives a grid of pixels, each with a brightness and colour.

skills.label: Image thresholding
skills.def: A single brightness cutoff splits an image into 'interesting' and 'not'.

skills.label: Blob detection
skills.def: Grouping connected matching pixels finds the object you are looking for.

skills.label: Centroid and area
skills.def: A blob's centre tells you where the object is and its area tells you how big.

skills.label: Line following by camera
skills.def: A camera can find and follow a line by locating it in each frame.

skills.label: Why vision breaks
skills.def: Light, shadow, colour shifts and blur can all fool a vision program.

skills.label: Rules vs learning
skills.def: When hand-written rules stop scaling, you learn behaviour from data instead.

skills.label: Features
skills.def: A feature is a measured number that describes an example for the machine to learn from.

skills.label: Labels
skills.def: A label is the correct answer attached to an example so the machine can learn it.

skills.label: A tiny classifier
skills.def: A classifier looks at features and predicts which labelled class an example belongs to.

skills.label: Train/test split
skills.def: Hold back some data to test on, so you measure learning and not memorising.

skills.label: Overfitting
skills.def: Scoring perfectly on training data but failing on new data means it just memorised.

skills.label: Where data comes from
skills.def: Training data reflects choices and biases that shape what a robot learns.

skills.label: Autonomy and responsibility
skills.def: When a machine decides on its own, someone is still responsible for what it does.

skills.label: Autonomous-machine safety
skills.def: A robot that acts on its own needs safety rules for when it gets things wrong.

skills.label: System architecture
skills.def: A robot is split into parts with clear jobs instead of one giant program.

skills.label: Messages between parts
skills.def: Parts of a robot talk by sending messages, like nodes and topics in ROS 2.

skills.label: Latency
skills.def: Messages take time to arrive, and that delay can ruin timing-sensitive behaviour.

skills.label: Reliability
skills.def: A robust system plans for the parts that will fail, like power loss or a stuck sensor.

skills.label: Test plans
skills.def: A test plan lists what to check so a robot survives a demo instead of failing live.

skills.label: Engineering process
skills.def: Engineering is a loop of specify, build the smallest test, measure, and revise.
